ClusterSettings.description: Overrides for one cluster: the per-cluster settings (display name, colour, read-only, default namespace, terminal directory, node shell, Prometheus, accessible namespaces, exec policy) and any other setting. Layers merge field by field: defaults, then the top-level values, then this block.

accessible_namespaces.description:
Namespaces to offer in the selector when the user is not allowed to list namespaces
cluster-wide (RBAC-restricted users). A list in a cluster replaces the one above it.

colour.description: Accent colour of the cluster's tab, hotbar dot and badges, as `#rrggbb` or `#rgb`.

confirm_quit.description:
Ask before quitting (or closing the last window on Linux and Windows) while exec sessions,
port-forwards or applies are running.

default_namespace.description: The namespace a new session starts in. Unset uses the kubeconfig context's namespace.

display_name.description:
A name to show instead of the kubeconfig context name. Cluster ids are opaque hashes, so
keep this next to the id to recognise the entry.

exec_interactivity.description:
How interactive exec credential plugins (`aws`, `gke-gcloud-auth-plugin`, ...) may be:
`never` (no stdin, never prompt; the GUI default), `if_available` or `always`. Read when a
session connects: a change takes effect on the next connect.

node_shell_image.description: Container image of the node shell pod. Unset uses the built-in image.

node_shell_pull_secret.description:
Name of the image pull Secret (in the node shell's namespace) used to pull
`node_shell_image` from a private registry. It names a Kubernetes Secret, it is not a
credential.

prometheus.description: Manual Prometheus location; unset auto-detects. Fields merge across layers.

read_only.description:
Block every mutation (create, edit, delete, scale, exec, node shell) for the cluster.
Set it under `clusters.<id>` to protect one cluster, or at the top level to start every
cluster read-only and opt individual ones out with `false`.

reduce_motion.description: `system` follows the OS reduce-motion preference, `on` and `off` override it.

terminal_cwd.description: Working directory of terminals opened for the cluster. Unset uses the home directory.

ui_scale.description:
UI zoom factor: 1.0 is 100 %. Values outside 0.5 to 3.0 are clamped. `cmd +`, `cmd -` and
`cmd 0` (`ctrl` elsewhere) change it and write it back here.

ClusterSettingsContent.description:
What one settings layer says about a cluster.

`display_name` and `colour` only make sense under `clusters.<id>`; at the top level they act
as a fallback for every cluster. Changes to `read_only`, `colour` and `display_name` reach
open sessions immediately; `exec_interactivity` is read when a session connects, so it takes
effect on the next connect; `default_namespace` is the namespace a session starts in, so it
does not move a selection the user already made.

Example, in `settings.json`:

```json
"clusters": {
  "3f2a9c1b7d4e8a60": {
    "display_name": "Production (eu-west)",
    "colour": "#e5484d",
    "read_only": true,
    "default_namespace": "payments",
    "prometheus": { "url": "https://prometheus.example.com", "auth_secret": "prod-prometheus" }
  }
}
```

terminal_cwd.description: Working directory of terminals opened for the cluster. Unset uses the home directory.

oneOf.description: deskribe for every kind it covers, `kubectl describe` for the rest (when installed).
deskribe only: a kind it does not cover is reported as unsupported.

DescribeSettingsContent.description: What one settings layer says about describe: the `describe` object of `settings.json`.

backend.description: `auto` (deskribe, then `kubectl` for a kind it does not cover), `native` or `kubectl`.

kubectl_path.description: Path of the `kubectl` binary; unset looks `kubectl` up on `PATH`.

HttpUrl.description: An http(s) URL without credentials, query or fragment.

KubeconfigSettingsContent.description: What one settings layer says about kubeconfig sources.

sources.description:
The kubeconfig files and folders to read, in order: the first definition of a context
name wins. `{ "kind": "default" }` is `KUBECONFIG`, else `~/.kube/config`;
`{ "kind": "file", "path": "..." }` and `{ "kind": "dir", "path": "..." }` add your own.
This list replaces the default list as a whole, so keep the `default` entry if you
still want kubectl's files.

path.description: The file or folder. A leading `~` is your home directory. Not used by `default`.

KubeconfigSourceKind.description: What a list entry points at.

oneOf.description: What kubectl reads: `KUBECONFIG`, else `~/.kube/config`. Takes no `path`.
One kubeconfig file, read where it is.
A folder of kubeconfig files (the files directly inside it).

LogSettingsContent.description: What one settings layer says about logging.

filter.description:
Log filter in `RUST_LOG` syntax, for example `info,oxikube_kube=debug`. Keep the HTTP
stack (hyper, h2, tower, rustls) at `warn` or quieter: at debug and trace they log request
headers (the writer redacts them, but they are noise). A `RUST_LOG` set at launch takes
precedence for that run.

LogsContent.description: What one settings layer says about logs: the `logs` object of `settings.json`.

buffer_lines.description:
Lines each log session keeps in memory (100 to 5,000,000; out of range is clamped). When
a chatty pod writes more, the oldest lines are dropped and the viewer shows a "truncated"
marker above the first one. A change applies to open sessions at once; set it under
`clusters.<id>.logs` to give one cluster a different bound.

default_tail.description:
Lines the tail range (key `0`) reads before it follows (1 to 100,000; out of range is
clamped). Applies to log views opened afterwards.

json_auto_detect.description:
JSON mode (key `j` toggles it per view): render the lines that are JSON objects as level /
time / message columns with expandable fields and the level chips; plain-text lines stay
as they are. A change applies to open views at once.

max_streams.description:
Containers a multi-pod log (a Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job or Service) reads at
once (1 to 200). When more match, the first are read in name order and the view says how
many pods were left out. A change applies to open views at once: a higher value starts
the pods that were left out.

timestamps.description:
Show each line's server timestamp before its text (key `t` toggles it per view). A change
applies to open views at once.

wrap.description:
Wrap long lines instead of letting them run off the edge (key `w` toggles it per view).
A change applies to open views at once.

PrometheusContent.description:
A manual Prometheus location for a cluster (`prometheus` key). Keeps no secret: the bearer
token lives in the OS keychain and `auth_secret` only names its entry.

auth_secret.description:
Name of the keychain entry (namespace `prometheus`) that holds the bearer token. Never
put the token itself in `settings.json`.

path.description: `namespace/service:port`, reached through the API server's service proxy.

provider.description:
`auto` (probe the cluster) or a provider id such as `operator`, `lens`, `helm`,
`victoria_metrics`, `mimir`. Unset means auto-detect.

url.description: A direct `http(s)` URL, used instead of `path`. No credentials, query or fragment.

oneOf.description: Follow the operating system's reduce-motion preference.
Always reduce motion, whatever the OS says.
Never reduce motion, whatever the OS says.

ResourceTableContent.description:
What one settings layer says about resource tables: the `resource_table` object of
`settings.json`.

persist_filter.description:
Remember the filter typed in each kind's table (the `/` bar) and restore it the next time
that table opens, like Freelens' persistent search. Off by default: a filter you forgot
about is a table that looks empty. The filter text is saved per kind (not per cluster).

RestoreConnectSetting.description: Which restored clusters connect at launch (`session.restore_connect`).

oneOf.description: Only the cluster whose tab was displayed; the others connect when their tab is first shown.
Every restored cluster, the displayed one first, two at a time.

SecretName.description: The name of a keychain entry holding the token. Never the token itself.

SessionRestoreContent.description: What one settings layer says about session restore: the `session` object of `settings.json`.

restore.description:
Reopen the clusters, tabs and namespaces of the last session at launch. Off by default.
Clusters connect after the window is up, and a cluster that fails or is unreachable only
shows an error in its own tab.

restore_connect.description:
Which restored clusters connect at launch: `active` (the one that was displayed; the others
connect when you open their tab) or `all`.

SessionSettingsContent.description: What one settings layer says about the session.

confirm_quit.description:
Ask before quitting (or closing the last window on Linux and Windows) while exec sessions,
port-forwards or applies are running.

reduce_motion.description: `system` follows the OS reduce-motion preference, `on` and `off` override it.

ui_scale.description:
UI zoom factor: 1.0 is 100 %. Values outside 0.5 to 3.0 are clamped. `cmd +`, `cmd -` and
`cmd 0` (`ctrl` elsewhere) change it and write it back here.

TerminalContent.description: What one settings layer says about terminals: the `terminal` object of `settings.json`.

confirm_multiline_paste.description:
Ask before pasting text with more than one line (default `true`): a pasted newline runs
the line. Single-line pastes never ask.

copy_on_select.description:
Copy the selection to the clipboard as soon as the mouse button is released (default
`false`). `cmd-c` (`ctrl-shift-c` elsewhere) always copies the selection explicitly, and
`ctrl-c` always reaches the process as an interrupt.

option_as_meta.description:
Whether Alt (Option) sends `ESC` before the key, the "meta" prefix shells and editors use
for `alt-b`, `alt-f`, `alt-.`. `null` (the default) is `false` on macOS, where Option
types characters (`å`, `∫`), and `true` elsewhere.

scrollback_lines.description: Lines of history each terminal keeps in memory (0 - 100000). Never saved to disk.

shell.description:
The shell a local terminal runs (a path or a name found on `PATH`). `null` uses the
`SHELL` environment variable, then `/bin/sh`. Applies to terminals opened afterwards.

shell_args.description:
Arguments passed to the shell, e.g. `["-l"]` for a login shell. Empty by default: a
login shell re-reads the profile files and slows opening a terminal, so it is only
started when you ask for it here.

ThemeMode.description: How the `theme` setting picks between a light and a dark theme.

anyOf.description: One theme, whatever the system appearance.
A light and a dark theme with a mode choosing between them.

dark.description: The theme to use in dark appearance.

light.description: The theme to use in light appearance.

ThemeSelectionContent.description: What one settings layer says about the theme.
